```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# rm(list=ls())

### Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(MuMIn)
library(rje)
library(parallel)
library(forcats)
library(sjPlot)
library(sjmisc)
library(sjlabelled)
library(performance)
library(doParallel)
library(foreach)
library(data.table)

### Read in and clean data
traits = read_csv("Data/speciesTraits/allparks_speclist_20220124 traits.csv")

# Quadrat-level species cover (zero-filled for surveyed quadrats), cleaned the same way as the species-level data
veg = read_csv("Data/IntermediateData/all_1x1veg_w0s_final.csv") |>
  merge(traits) |>
  filter(!str_detect(sciname," sp$")) |>
  filter(tax_unit!="lichen"&habit!="clubmoss"&habit!="fern"&habit!="tree"&perennating!="annual")

# Summit-aspect-transition climate and site latitude from the species-level data
# only drop site groups missing climate PCs -- no species-level filters here
site.dats = read_csv('Data/AnalysisData/specieslevel_analysisdata_final.csv') |>
  select(park,summit,aspect,transition,startyear,endyear,sitelat,starts_with(c("climPC","min.","mean.","max."))) |>
  distinct() |>
  drop_na(climPC1,climPC2)

mod.dats = site.dats |>
  select(summit,aspect,transition,startyear,endyear) |>
  inner_join(select(veg,summit,aspect,plot,habit,startyear=year,sciname,startcover=cover),by=c("summit","aspect","startyear")) |>
  inner_join(select(veg,summit,aspect,plot,endyear=year,sciname,endcover=cover),by=c("summit","aspect","plot","endyear","sciname")) |>
  # filter(habit %in% c("forb","gram")) |>
  filter(habit != "tree") |>
  group_by(summit,aspect,plot,transition) |>
  summarise(start.nspp = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover > 0)]),
            end.nspp = n_distinct(sciname[which(endcover > 0)]),
            
            start.n.forbs = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover > 0 & habit=="forb")]),
            end.n.forbs = n_distinct(sciname[which(endcover > 0 & habit=="forb")]),
            change.forbs = end.n.forbs - start.n.forbs,
            
            start.n.gram = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover > 0 & habit=="gram")]),
            end.n.gram = n_distinct(sciname[which(endcover > 0 & habit=="gram")]),
            change.gram = end.n.gram - start.n.gram,
            
            shared = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover > 0 & endcover > 0)]),
            gains = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover == 0 & endcover > 0)]),
            losses = n_distinct(sciname[which(startcover > 0 & endcover == 0)]),

            # Reviewer 1 #3: compositional change using species cover (Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between start and end survey; 0 = identical, 1 = no shared cover)
            bc.dissim = sum(abs(endcover - startcover)) / sum(startcover + endcover),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(change.nspp = end.nspp - start.nspp,
         turnover = (gains + losses) / (shared + gains + losses), # Reviewer 1 #3 & Reviewer 2: proportion of species gained or lost (Jaccard dissimilarity)
         tr.num = as.numeric(substr(transition,4,4))) |>
  merge(site.dats,by=c("summit","aspect","transition")) |>
  mutate(parksummit = paste(park,summit,sep="."),
         PSaspect = paste(park,summit,aspect,sep="."),
         PSaspect.plot = paste(park,summit,aspect,plot,sep="."),
         quadrat = paste(park,summit,plot,sep="."),
         quad.trans = paste0(quadrat,".",tr.num))

mod.dats$park = factor(mod.dats$park,levels=c("GNP","YNP","RMN","GSD","PEC"))

run.date <- Sys.Date()

### Create another dataframe where numeric predictor variables are scaled ###
dats.scaled = mod.dats # Get names columns to standardize
scale_cols = mod.dats %>% select(start.nspp,climPC1,climPC2,sitelat,contains(c(".tmean",".aet",".pet",".ppt",".snowdays",".gdd"))) %>% names()
dats.scaled[scale_cols]=lapply(dats.scaled[scale_cols], function(x) scale(x))

rm(scale_cols)
```

## Did richness change overall and by park?
```{r direction_test_richness}
# Reviewer 1 (minor comment: "a simple analysis to test if richness increased") & Reviewer 2 (general comment on richness)
# Intercept = mean change in number of species per quadrat; CI excluding 0 = systematic change
nspp.mod = lmer(change.nspp ~ 1 + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(nspp.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")

# By park
nspp.park.mod = lmer(change.nspp ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(nspp.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
```

## Are forbs and graminoids increasing or decreasing?
```{r direction_test}
# Editor & Reviewer 1 (line 27): community-level check on species-level result that graminoids increased more than forbs
# Intercept = mean change in number of species per quadrat; CI excluding 0 = systematic change
forb.mod = lmer(change.forbs ~ 1 + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
gram.mod = lmer(change.gram ~ 1 + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(forb.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
confint(gram.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")

# By park
forb.park.mod = lmer(change.forbs ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
gram.park.mod = lmer(change.gram ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(forb.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
confint(gram.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
```

## How much species turnover is there, by park?
```{r turnover}
# Reviewer 1 #3 (turnover not quantified) & Reviewer 2 (general comment on species gains and losses)
# Mean number of species gained and lost per quadrat, by park
gains.park.mod = lmer(gains ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
losses.park.mod = lmer(losses ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(gains.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
confint(losses.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")

# Turnover based on presence/absence (proportion of species gained or lost) and on cover (Bray-Curtis)
turnover.park.mod = lmer(turnover ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
bc.park.mod = lmer(bc.dissim ~ 0 + park + (1|transition), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)
confint(turnover.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
confint(bc.park.mod, parm = "beta_", method = "Wald")
```

## Model selection for change in richness (steps 1-4)
Reviewer 1 (minor comment on richness) & Reviewer 2 (general comment): the "simple models" of change in species richness, built with the same model selection procedure as the species-level models

1. Find random effect structure
```{r REstructure}

###### Full fixed effects model before any winnowing of FE variables #######

mod1 <- lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|PSaspect),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod2 <- lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|transition),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod3 <- lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|quadrat),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod4 <- lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|PSaspect) + (1|transition),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod5 <- lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|quadrat) + (1|transition),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

AICc(mod1)
AICc(mod2)
AICc(mod3)
AICc(mod4)
AICc(mod5)

## Mod 2 is the best model here (mod4 is singular -- quadrat variance estimated at 0)
# AICc(mod1) 2339.66
# AICc(mod2) 2326.31
# AICc(mod3) 2345.11
# AICc(mod4) 2327.52
# AICc(mod5) 2328.41
```


2. Find fixed structure with climate PCs 1 & 2 #####
Refit best RE model using ML + dredge to find the most important fixed effects
```{r FEstructure_refitwithML_thenDredge}

# Refit using ML rather than REML
climPC.RE.mod.MLfit = lmer(end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(climPC1+climPC2+sitelat) + (1|transition),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = FALSE)
climPC.RE.mod.MLfit %>% summary()

climPC.RE.mod.dredge = dredge(climPC.RE.mod.MLfit, beta = c("none"), fixed = c('start.nspp'),trace=2)

best.climPC.fe.mod = get.models(climPC.RE.mod.dredge,subset = 1)[[1]]
top10.climPC.fe.mods = get.models(climPC.RE.mod.dredge,subset = 1:10)

saveRDS(object = list(bestMod = best.climPC.fe.mod,top10.climPC.fe.mods = top10.climPC.fe.mods),
        file = paste0("Results/climPC_models_richness_",run.date,".rds"))

climPC.RE.mod.dredge.fltr = as.data.frame(climPC.RE.mod.dredge) %>% slice_head(n = 10)
write_csv(climPC.RE.mod.dredge.fltr,paste0("Results/climPC_richness_dredge_results_",run.date,".csv"))
```

3. Take that model with the optimal FE and RE structure find best explicit climate variables in nested loops
```{r best.clim.vars}

best.climPC.mods <- readRDS(paste0("Results/climPC_models_richness_",run.date,".rds"))
best.climPC.mod = best.climPC.mods$bestMod
summary(best.climPC.mod)

# Replace climPC1/2 with generic clim var names
climVar.generic.mod = c("end.nspp ~ start.nspp*(sitelat + tmean.var + cwd.var + ppt.var + snow.gdd.var) + (1 | transition)")

# Create climate variable variable groups
val = c("min","max","mean")
tmean.grp = append(paste0(val,".tmean"),NA)
snow.gdd.grp = append(c(paste0(val,".gdd"),paste0(val,".snowdays")),NA)
ppt.grp = append(paste0(val,".gs.ppt"),NA)
cwd.grp =  append(c(paste0(val,".aet"),paste0(val,".pet"),paste0(val,".wy.ppt")),NA)
rm(val)

climVar_param_grid <- expand_grid(tmean.grp,snow.gdd.grp,ppt.grp,cwd.grp) %>%
  filter(!if_all(everything(), is.na))

# In each iteration, a single climate variable from each group is subbed in for the generic climate variables above (i.e., tmean.var is swapped out for mean.tmean). That model is then fit with ML (not REML) and the AIC value is stored in the output table for comparison once the loops are finished running

#### Initiate cluster #####
clust = makeCluster(spec = 2)
registerDoParallel(cl = clust)

results_list <- foreach::foreach(i = 1:nrow(climVar_param_grid), .packages = c("tidyverse","data.table","lme4","performance","MuMIn") )%dopar%{
  
  row.i <- climVar_param_grid[i,]
  
  tmean.i <- row.i$tmean.grp
  cwd.i <- row.i$cwd.grp
  ppt.i <- row.i$ppt.grp
  snow.gdd.i <- row.i$snow.gdd.grp
  
  clim.mod.i = climVar.generic.mod 
  
  # either remove tmean.var or replace with specific tmean variable name. Repeat the same process for all other clim variable groups
  if(is.na(tmean.i)) {clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "tmean.var + ",replacement = "", x = clim.mod.i, fixed = T)
  }else{clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "tmean.var",replacement = tmean.i,x = clim.mod.i)}
  
  if(is.na(cwd.i)) {clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "cwd.var + ",replacement = "", x = clim.mod.i, fixed = T)
  }else{clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "cwd.var",replacement = cwd.i,x = clim.mod.i)}
          
  if(is.na(ppt.i)) {clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "ppt.var + ",replacement = "", x = clim.mod.i, fixed = T)
  }else{clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "ppt.var",replacement = ppt.i,x = clim.mod.i)}
  
  if(is.na(snow.gdd.i)) {clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = " + snow.gdd.var",replacement = "", x = clim.mod.i, fixed = T)
  }else{clim.mod.i = gsub(pattern = "snow.gdd.var",replacement = snow.gdd.i,x = clim.mod.i)}
  
  out_df = data.table(tmean.var = tmean.i,
            snow.gdd.var = snow.gdd.i,
            ppt.var = ppt.i,
            cwd.var = cwd.i,
            mod.str = clim.mod.i)
  
   # Fit in LMER
    mod.fit.i = lmer(formula = clim.mod.i, data = dats.scaled, REML = FALSE, na.action = "na.fail")

    out_df$AICc=AICc(mod.fit.i)
    out_df$condR2 = r2(mod.fit.i)[[1]]
    out_df$margR2 = r.squaredGLMM(mod.fit.i)[[1]]
    return(out_df)

}
stopCluster(clust)
clim.mod.AICs <- rbindlist(results_list)

clim.mod.AICs$delta = clim.mod.AICs$AICc - min(clim.mod.AICs$AICc)
clim.mod.AICs <- clim.mod.AICs %>% arrange(delta)

best.ExplClimVar.mod.str <- clim.mod.AICs$mod.str[clim.mod.AICs$delta==0]
best.ExplClimVar.mod.str
```


4. With the best climate variables, revisit random effect structure
```{r explClimVars.REs}

# Swap the random effects in the best explicit-climate model
mod1 <- lmer(sub("(1 | transition)", "(1|PSaspect)", best.ExplClimVar.mod.str, fixed = TRUE),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod2 <- lmer(best.ExplClimVar.mod.str,
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

mod3 <- lmer(sub("(1 | transition)", "(1|PSaspect) + (1|transition)", best.ExplClimVar.mod.str, fixed = TRUE),
             na.action = "na.fail",data = dats.scaled,REML = TRUE)

AICc(mod1)
AICc(mod2)
AICc(mod3)

# Save best explicit-climate model (mod2, REML fit) and the full climate-variable AICc table
saveRDS(object = list(bestMod = mod2, clim.mod.AICs = clim.mod.AICs),
        file = paste0("Results/climVar_models_richness_",run.date,".rds"))
write_csv(clim.mod.AICs,paste0("Results/climVar_richness_AICc_results_",run.date,".csv"))
```


```{r plots}
# Best explicit-climate model
richMod <- readRDS("Results/climVar_models_richness_2026-10-20.rds")[[1]]
summary(richMod)
sjPlot::plot_model(richMod)
sjPlot::plot_model(richMod,type="pred")
sjPlot::plot_model(richMod,type="int")

# Predicted change (predicted end - start) at the actual data points, each with its own climate and start richness
richMod.us = lmer(formula(richMod), data = mod.dats, REML = TRUE)   # refit on unscaled data

rich_pred_df = mod.dats %>%
  mutate(pred.endnspp = predict(richMod.us, newdata = ., re.form = NA),
         pred.changenspp = pred.endnspp - start.nspp,
         park2 = case_when(park=="GNP"~"GLAC",
                           park=="YNP"~"YELL",
                           park=="RMN"~"ROMO",
                           park=="GSD"~"GRSD",
                           park=="PEC"~"PECO"),
         park2 = factor(park2,levels=rev(c("GLAC","YELL","ROMO","GRSD","PECO"))))

park.pal = c(GLAC='#B07AA1',YELL='#1170AA',ROMO='#59A14F',GRSD='#E6AB02',PECO='#C85200')

ggplot(rich_pred_df, aes(x = start.nspp, y = pred.changenspp, color = park2)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method="lm")+
  scale_color_manual(values = park.pal) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
  labs(x = "Start richness", y = "Predicted change in richness", color = "Park")
```


## SCRATCH
### Ordination of community composition (for learning, not for the manuscript)
Each point is one summit-aspect survey; arrows connect consecutive surveys (one arrow = one transition). Arrow length = how much composition changed (same idea as bc.dissim)
```{r scratch_nmds}
library(vegan)

# Mean cover of each species in each summit-aspect survey (averaged across quadrats)
comm.wide = veg %>%
  group_by(park,summit,aspect,year,sciname) %>%
  summarise(cover = mean(cover), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sciname, values_from = cover, values_fill = 0)

comm.mat = comm.wide %>% select(-c(park,summit,aspect,year)) # species x survey matrix

set.seed(1)
comm.nmds = metaMDS(comm.mat, distance = "bray", k = 2, trymax = 50)
comm.nmds$stress # < 0.2 is generally considered acceptable

nmds.df = comm.wide %>%
  select(park,summit,aspect,year) %>%
  mutate(NMDS1 = comm.nmds$points[,1],
         NMDS2 = comm.nmds$points[,2],
         park2 = case_when(park=="GNP"~"GLAC",
                           park=="YNP"~"YELL",
                           park=="RMN"~"ROMO",
                           park=="GSD"~"GRSD",
                           park=="PEC"~"PECO"),
         park2 = factor(park2,levels=rev(c("GLAC","YELL","ROMO","GRSD","PECO")))) %>%
  arrange(park,summit,aspect,year) %>%
  group_by(park,summit,aspect) %>%
  mutate(NMDS1.next = lead(NMDS1), NMDS2.next = lead(NMDS2)) %>% # position at next survey
  ungroup()

park.pal = c(GLAC='#B07AA1',YELL='#1170AA',ROMO='#59A14F',GRSD='#E6AB02',PECO='#C85200')

ggplot(nmds.df, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = park2)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = NMDS1.next, yend = NMDS2.next), arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.15,"cm")), na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = park.pal) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(color = "Park")
```
